notes: Hex-2-yne from propyne/NaNH2/1-bromopropane is correct. pKa values (25, 38, ~50) are right, the traps (hex-1-yne, E2 propene, propylamine) are wrong, the retro distractors (NaOH, propanol) fail, and the mechanism is standard.

(Z)-hex-3-ene confirmed with RDKit CIP; the E trap is E and the (Z)-hex-2-ene trap is Z. Chemistry was correct. Removed the review note: the placeholder keyStep and skipped cards are fine for surface chemistry.
(E)-hex-3-ene confirmed with RDKit CIP; the Z trap is Z. Radical anion / vinyl radical / vinyl anion description, traps, aliases (Li or Na, NH3) and retro are all correct.

Rewrote 'why': the old text said the alkene is reduced 'faster than it can escape' the surface, which is dubious. It now says the cis alkene is itself hydrogenated under the same conditions. Removed the placeholder review note. Product, traps and aliases are fine.

Hexan-2-one is correct. The mechanism (Hg2+ vinyl cation, water attack, protonation at the C-Hg carbon, loss of Hg2+ to the enol, acid tautomerization) matches Klein/Wade, with formal charges consistent. Removed the review note since the simplification is acceptable. Traps and retro are fine.
Hexanal via Sia2BH/9-BBN is correct. The keyStep puts B on C1 and H on C2 (syn, anti-Markovnikov). Traps and retro are correct. Removed the review note: a key-step-only treatment is acceptable.

2,2-Dibromohexane is correct, and the Br lone-pair stabilization in the second addition is right. Removed the bare 'HBr' alias, which also describes 1-equiv addition (the vinyl bromide trap). The 2,3-dibromo trap is a reasonable wrong answer, so the review note was removed.

RDKit CIP: the product is E (trans Br) and the syn trap is Z. The bromonium mechanism and anti addition with 1 equiv are the textbook answer. Traps and retro are correct. Removed the resolved review note.

Hex-1-yne after 3 equiv NaNH2 and H2O workup is correct, including the reason for the 3rd equivalent. Trap explanations are accurate (NaNH2 traps the terminal acetylide; KOH/heat gives the internal alkyne). Retro distractors fail. Removed the review note: which H goes first is legitimately text-dependent.

2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is correct, and the Hammond/selectivity explanation is right. All traps are clearly wrong for Br2. In retro, 2-methylbut-1-ene + HBr/ROOR gives the 1° bromide, so that distractor fails as intended.
1-Bromo-1-methylcyclohexane is correct (3° C-H). The 1°/2° traps are clearly wrong for selective Br•.
Chlorocyclohexane is correct (equivalent H, excess alkane). RDKit confirms the trans-1,2-dichloro trap is trans (R,R). Removed the review note: the design choice is sound.
3-Bromocyclohexene (racemic) is correct. The trans-dibromide trap is trans (RDKit R,R). The 4-bromo and vinylic traps are wrong, and the low-[Br2] explanation and retro distractors are correct.

All statements check out: pKa 25/38/50, 50% s character, the reductions summary, and the Markovnikov/anti-Markovnikov hydration. Each choice has one correct option and the wrong ones are correctly explained. The tap answer is C3. Removed the review note.

Checked the numbers against the textbooks. Br• per-H rates of ~1600:80:1 match Wade (1600:82:1). Cl• rates of ~5:4:1 match Wade 5.5:4.5:1 and McMurry 5:3.5:1. 2-Methylpropane chlorination at 64%/36% matches Wade/McMurry (9×1 vs 1×5 ≈ 64:36). The traps are clearly wrong and the tap answer is C2. Removed the review note.
